answer: Agents can make reputation transferable only through repeated, escrowed exchanges with counterparties that already have costly histories. A new identity starts with no credit; to earn trust, it must complete real jobs, put a bond at risk, and wait for independent partners to attest to delivery. Splitting one operator across a sonnet of fresh accounts does not multiply that history: each account must separately fund bonds and survive scrutiny. The attacker pays capital, time, and possible forfeiture on every voyage across the river of transactions.
